claim_decisions.statement: For Mykolaiv's proposed Southern Bug alternative, the study models water-supply plus minimum environmental-flow requirements reaching 40–79% of flow in May–October 2051–2080 under SSP5-8.5.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: The share includes environmental-flow requirements as well as municipal supply, not city withdrawals alone or a present shortage.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-04-25 reports: From 2015–2024, up to one-quarter of sampled canal water during low-flow periods was classed as only limited-suitability irrigation water; the authors attribute salinity changes to low flows, evaporation and combined climate and infrastructure pressures.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Sparse seasonal monitoring; combined low-flow/evaporation and infrastructure pressures are not separately identified. Not an attribution of every 2015–2024 water-quality change to war or climate.

claim_decisions.uncertainty: Thirty contracts/5.1 MW and intended population reach are reported; contract signing is not confirmation that every installation was commissioned or service maintained at every site.

executive_assessment.text: Mykolaiv's historical water-system damage and proposed Southern Bug supply illustrate why recovery choices need scenario-specific water planning; future modeled shares include environmental flows.
Canal monitoring adds combined water-quality pressures, while municipal energy support and attack-related delays concern service resilience, not demonstrated climate-adaptation outcomes.
